html:
The Alta controversy was a protest from 1979 to 1982 against a dam on the Alta river in northern Norway, which would flood land used by Sámi reindeer herders.

Sámi activists and environmentalists chained themselves at the building site, and some went on hunger strike in front of parliament in Oslo. The state sent hundreds of police to clear the camp. The dam was built in a smaller form.

But the protests changed how Norway treated the Sámi. For a century policy had aimed at making them Norwegian, banning their language in schools. After Alta the constitution was changed to protect Sámi culture, and a Sámi Parliament opened in 1989. Norway also signed the international convention on indigenous peoples in 1990.
sum: The Alta controversy was a protest from 1979 to 1982 against a dam on the Alta river in northern Norway, which would flood land used by Sámi reindeer herders.
